Nobody sets out to write a negative review but....||To be completely fair, Villa Song was our last stay on an incredible tour of Malaysia, Cambodia and Vietnam, which until then had seen us visit some remarkable places (more in other reviews), so it was inevitably compared with very high quality experiences. Sadly, it fell way short.||Arrival wasn't encouraging, along a dirty street dominated by roadworks and crawling traffic due to school runs. The hotel itself is a little past its (no doubt once magnificent) best, with dead or dying flowers in pots, ageing upholstery and a general air of faded grandeur, though its location on the river is excellent. Reception is in a poorly lit room with staff who struggled to communicate. OK - my Vietnamese is non existent but this represents itself as an international venue and nowhere else had we come across this so a bit surprising. On the positive side, the bell boy was excellent, carting heavy cases up steep stairs (no lift). ||The room, best in the hotel, apparently, was similarly dingy and rather bare. Quality of towels, bed linen etc second rate. Coffee machine didn't work, so we used the sachets provided then called to ask for a refill. No coffee sachets in the hotel, apparently. Really? It's a small point but there were no flowers in the room and the balcony furniture was at best functional. This is represented as a luxury hotel. It is not.||We didn't eat dinner there and in fairness the recommended alternative restaurant was ok. We did eat breakfast which was, frankly, rubbish: rubbery, white bread and yoghurt with granola nobody asked for, plus mediocre fruit.  We asked for sourdough toast and were told it would take a week (!), despite there being several what looked like very pleasant bakeries close by. The following day, granary bread miraculously turned up, in the form of rolls. We appreciated the effort but not what we asked for.||Next day we took the boat into town. Please note, this is, literally, once a day, not the shuttle service implied. Except it isn't. The 1630 return never arrived. After various calls, it was sent and came an hour later. The boat ride is fun but this was unimpressive.||When we asked for a car to the airport for our departure the day before leaving we were told that we had booked for three nights, not two. Our mistake - no question. Just a diary mix up. Refund for the night not used requested and refused, by WhatsApp message! I could easily understand if the hotel was full but it seemed to us to be very far from busy. And given the fact that we had made our unhappiness clear, it might have been sensible for someone to at least speak with us but no: policy, apparently.||So, and it is easy to allow that refusal to colour everything (the mistake was ours and nobody else's), a disappointing end to a fabulous trip. From what we could see, there are many, many good alternatives to Villa Song. Were we ever to go back to Ho Chi Minh City, we wouldn't even consider Villa Song and neither should anyone else in our view.

This has become our go-to place whenever we’re craving great Vietnamese food. The Hoi An-inspired setting is absolutely beautiful, with colourful lanterns, charming décor, and a peaceful pond filled with fish that creates a relaxing and authentic atmosphere.

The food is consistently delicious, but the Vietnamese salad is the standout for me. It’s incredibly fresh and refreshing, with the perfect balance of tangy, sweet, savoury, and crunchy flavours. I look forward to ordering it every time we visit.

It’s also a wonderful place for families. Seeing children happily playing around gives the restaurant a warm and lively atmosphere, and the picturesque surroundings make it easy to spend time taking photos.

The staff are genuinely friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even more memorable.

The only small downside was that we got bitten by a few mosquitoes while sitting indoors, probably because of the open-air design and the nearby pond. It wasn’t enough to spoil the experience, but it’s something to be aware of.

Update: We’ve now been back twice since our first visit, and every experience has been just as enjoyable. The food, service, and atmosphere have remained consistently excellent, making this our default choice for Vietnamese food. Highly recommended!
